To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conditional phase averaging of the subgrid scale (SGS) stress tensor in a turbulent shear flow reveals a significant dependence of the stress-strain-rate tensor alignment on the phase, i.e. on the large-scale coherent structures.
coherent structures have a profound effect on the subgrid scale (SGS) stress and strain-rate tensor alignments, and that the most likely alignment angle is a strong function of the flow topology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of large-scale coherent structure on the alignment of subgrid-scale (SGS) stresses and strains.
the effects of large-scale structures on the small-scale dynamics.
the effect of coherent structures on the subgrid-scale stress-strain rate tensor alignment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of coherent structures on subfilter-scale stress-strain alignments is to increase the alignment in the vortex centers and decrease the alignment in the straining regions, as well as to reduce the magnitude of the subgrid stress tensor.
the subgrid-scale stress-strain-rate alignment depends on the flow and the Reynolds number and that it can be affected by the presence of large scale coherent structures.

, for a turbulent flow with large-scale coherent structures (such as the flows considered in this study), the subgrid scale (SGS) stress and strain-rate tensor are not aligned in the inertial range, but that the SGS stress and strain-rate are better aligned in the presence of a similarity term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, the effects of large-scale coherent structure on subgrid-scale (SGS) stress-strain tensor alignment are studied.
, in turbulent shear flow, the subgrid scale (SGS) stress-strain-rate tensor alignment depends strongly on the presence of large-scale coherent vortices and the associated strain-rate field.
the large-scale coherent structures have significant effects on the subgrid-scale stress-strain-rate eigenvector alignment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the inertial range of turbulence, subgrid-scale stress alignment with the local strain-rate tensor is not as good as previously believed.
the large scale coherent structures in turbulent shear flow are responsible for the misalignment of the subgrid-scale stress with the strain-rate.
the subgrid scale stresses are not aligned with the most extensive eigenstrain-rate vector at the vortices, and that the subgrid scales are not isotropic.
